organization: International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC)
description:
What we do
 
The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) works worldwide to provide protection and humanitarian assistance to people affected by conflict and armed violence. We take action in response to emergencies and, at the same time, promote respect for international humanitarian law. We are an independent and neutral organization, and our mandate stems essentially from the Geneva Conventions of 1949. We work closely with National Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies and with their International Federation in order to ensure a concerted, rational and rapid humanitarian response to the needs of the victims of armed conflict or any other situation of internal violence. We direct and coordinate the international activities conducted in these situations.
 Purpose
 
The Movement Cooperation officer contributes to the planning, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of the Delegation’s Movement Cooperation objectives. He/she works under the supervision of the Movement Cooperation Coordinator (MCC).
This is a resident/National position based in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.
 Relationships
 

Internally, interacts with Movement Cooperation department, other departments and focal persons of sub-delegation
Externally, interacts with ERCS and other Movement partners.

 Accountabilities & functional responsibilities
 
Program Design, Implementation, and Evaluation
 

Supports relevant departments, sub-delegations, and the Ethiopian Red Cross Society (ERCS) in designing, implementing, monitoring, and evaluating joint programs.
Contributes to analyzing the context and humanitarian needs through regular contact with ERCS.
Ensures proper coordination of ICRC and ERCS plans and activities under Movement Cooperation and ICRC operational departments.

 
Collaboration and Partnership
 

Facilitates cooperation  and mutual understanding between ICRC and ERCS in the field to strengthen their partnership.
Strengthens ICRC coordination with ERCS and other Movement partners within the area of responsibility.
Builds and maintains positive relationships and trust between ICRC and ERCS.
Conducts periodic visits to ICRC sub-delegations and ERCS branches within the area of responsibility to foster regular coordination and ensure partnership modalities are understood and respected.

 
Capacity Building and Support
 

Contributes to ERCS capacity strengthening (National Society development) and supports ERCS priorities in line with the partnership between the two institutions.
Under the guidance of the Movement Cooperation Coordinator, supports ERCS in designing and implementing internal policies, systems, guidelines, and Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs).
In coordination with team members of the Movement Cooperation department and other ICRC departments, supports ERCS in emergency preparedness and response activities.
Organizes and facilitates trainings, workshops, and seminars in Addis Ababa and in the field.

 
 Accountabilities & functional responsibilities 2
 
Policy and Agreement Management
 

Participates in the reviews of Partnership Framework Agreements (PFA), Operational Cooperation Agreements (OCA), and other Movement-related agreements.
Promotes the Fundamental Principles across the delegation, sub-delegations, and Movement, while monitoring their implementation.
Follows up on and recommends measures for implementing decisions and resolutions from the Council of Delegates and Movement Statutory Meetings.

 
Monitoring and Reporting
 

Analyzes and shares insights on new developments within the Movement in Ethiopia.
Compiles, analyzes, and summarizes quarterly reports for distribution to relevant stakeholders.
Handles regular duties, including drafting meeting minutes, compiling periodic reports, managing internal tools and databases, and maintaining proper filing systems.

 
Administration – Finance
 

Knows, applies and complies with all the administrative and finance procedures.
In close consultation with the Administrative Assistant, reviews regular and ad-hoc financial requests from ERCS to ensure accuracy, compliance with established practices and standards, and alignment with agreed plans of action; provides recommendations for new requests and ensures timely payments.
Keeps files up to date at all times 

 
 Additional duties
 
Reporting
 

Ensures timely reporting of activities to Movement Cooperation Coordinator 

 
Translation and Communication
 

Translate documents between English and Amharic as required.

 
Other
 

Undertakes other tasks assigned by the Movement Cooperation Coordinator
EDUCATION, EXPERIENCE AND COMPETENCIES REQUIRED
 

Bachelor’s degree in international relations, Political Science, Law, Project Management, Business Administration, or equivalent qualification in a related field of study
Minimum of 3 years of work experience in Movement Cooperation or a similar field within or outside the Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement

title: Driver Light vehicles Driver Light vehicles Driver Light vehicles
organization: International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC)
description:
What we do
 
Since 1863, the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) has worked to preserve human dignity and relieve suffering caused by war and armed violence.In collaboration with our Red Cross and Red Crescent partners around the world, we do everything we can to deliver life-saving aid, reconnect families and locate missing people – helping those who need it most, regardless of who they are and what side of the front line they are on.We engage with authorities and armed forces on all sides, often confidentially, pressing for access to detainees to improve their living conditions and urging compliance with international humanitarian law to protect non-combatants, including from digital threats.
 Purpose
 

The Light Vehicles Driver transports people and goods in a safe and timely manner, in accordance with ICRC rules and regulations and national traffic laws.

 Relationships
 

Internally, interacts mainly with logistics staff and other ICRC employees.
Externally, interacts with people related to their work, e.g. traffic police, weapon bearers at checkpoints, fuel-station personnel, etc. May interact with beneficiaries.

 Accountabilities & functional responsibilities
 
Functional Responsibilities:
 

Drives light vehicles to transport people and/or material in strict adherence to internal security rules and national traffic laws.
Constantly monitors security conditions on the road.
Ensures that goods are stored inside the vehicle according to local, international and ICRC safety standards (attachment and distribution of goods, etc.).
Checks the assigned vehicle(s)' equipment, general functioning and body condition and ensures that it is kept fuelled and clean inside and out.
Checks validity of stickers for Local Third-party insurance coverage and MoT annual inspection.
Checks that trips have been authorized where necessary.
Immediately reports accidents, defects and/or missing equipment to management.
Can act as head of convoy as needed (in charge of the driver(s), application of security rules and timeframe for the convoy.

 ADDITIONAL DUTIES 
 
Transport
 

Delivers mail or goods as requested
Provide assistance to the passengers as needed

 
Security
 

Informs Radio room & Car Dispatcher about time of departure and return to the base
Makes sure that vehicle is parked in safe area in departure position all the time
Is aware of and reacts to the current security situation
Respects ICRC internal security rules all the time
Respects the laws in general and traffic regulations in particular
Use the safety belt and oblige passenger to use it
Drives only ICRC goods and personnel in ICRC vehicles unless instructed differently by superiors
Fills Waiver of liability when transporting non-ICRC passenger(s)
Fills in relevant field trip and other form
Avoids using mobile phones while driving and respects radio communication procedures
Is aware of the rules concerning correct use of vehicle, and carriage of passengers and goods
Acts as a convoy leader when required

 
Fuel
 

Ensures that the vehicles are always refuelled in time
Drives in a manner that minimizes fuel consumption and always maintains vehicle in good condition
Fills in refuelling data in logbook and fuel control sheets
Hands over any fuel bills to fleet data admin /dispatcher at the end of the trip
ADDITIONAL DUTIES 2
 
Load responsibility
 

When applicable, is present at the loading and unloading of goods and confirms that the quantity and corresponds with relevant documentation
Is responsible for goods documentation
During unloading presents documentation to the receiver of the goods to be signed and returns it to dispatcher or concerned personnel.
Participate in the loading and unloading of his vehicle

 
General
 

Drives in safe, responsible and accident-free manner
Adapts way of driving to the weather and road conditions
Reports to dispatcher about road conditions, eventual problems etc.
Reports vehicle accidents/crashes immediately using appropriate forms (including minor scratches)

 
Vehicle's checking & maintenance
 

During each handover and once a week checks vehicle equipment and body condition assigned using a checking list prepared for this purpose.
Is able to replace flat tyres or blown out bulbs on the way.
Is responsible for equipment, tools, chains, spare tyres and any driver essentials equipment placed in the vehicles and reports any missing to Car Dispatcher
Informs Car Dispatcher about service, maintenance and other possible repairs needed in advance and fills in technical report
During the trips monitors all cabin instruments to be able to promptly react if needed

 
 Others
 

Replaces other driver during their absence
Performs any other activities upon request of immediate supervisor
When required acts as translator or support a Field Officer or Delegate
Back-up the vehicle dispatcher
Flexibility and Willingness to work in irregular schedules
Shows a helpful and solution-oriented attitude
